The Soft Colors of a Summer Evening. It's a typical summer's evening on the shores of Bay Saint Louis, MS, and that's not a bad thing. The breaking waves almost lull you asleep with their constant low rumble, and the incoming seabreeze sets the temps down wonderfully into the low 70s. The pastel colors of the coast shine through late in the day on days like these. The incoming CSX train barely causes a stir, and aside from the horn sequence for Beach Boulevard, it goes almost entirely unnoticed. As M601 heads south, distant horn sequences grow lower and lower until they disappear. Just like that the low rumble of the Gulf takes back over, and a pleasant summer evening continues along the Mississippi Gulf Coast.

CN 79482 was one of 548 steel cabooses built by Canadian National Railway Company Pointe St. Charles shops in Montreal between 1970 and 1977 using boxcars as cores. It was used by CN as a shoving platform after retirement as a working  van. It was moved to Waterloo Central Railway in 2007, renumbered 482 and modified to carry passengers. It now proudly joins our train rides and creates ear-to-ear smiles on all that experience it's wonder.

The sound of four General Electric motors digging in fills the cool mountain air as BNSF 780 ducks under the signals at CP Walker. They started up Cajon with some gusto, but mother nature is fighting back. The grade and the tonnage on the drawbar now have the quartet earning their keep as they lug the West Colton to Barstow mixed freight toward Summit. 

I had started this day a bit irritated. I learned that I had missed some fun and very photo-worthy motive power. I decided, since I didn't catch the intended targets that I would swing by West Colton and just see what Uncle Pete and his gang had for me. I'm glad I did. I was able to chase the 'Wickle-Bar' from Colton until Hesperia.
